speaker: NARRATOR
text: Somewhere past Mars, a ship stopped answering.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Then a capsule fell back to Earth.

speaker: FATHER
text: They found the capsule. I keep thinking he is alive.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The ship was his son's. So was the plan.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Nobody checked it. Ten percent. That was his chance.

speaker: PIP
text: I am Pip. I keep the count so you do not have to.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: One last known signal. One father with a second chance.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Fix the plan. Fly the ship. Bring him home.

speaker: PIP
text: Build a test frame on the sled. Pick an engine and only the payload this test needs, lock the clamps, then fire. Watch a = F / m.

speaker: PIP
text: Heavier frame, slower push: acceleration is thrust over mass. NASA Glenn, Beginner's Guide to Rockets.

speaker: PIP
text: Your son's flight assessment is in the records. It was never in his briefing.

speaker: PIP
text: Open it, then fix the plan in the Mission Planner. Every check runs against the plan you apply.

speaker: PIP
text: In this game, five 63% parts give 10%. Backups raise odds, cost mass. NASA Systems Engineering Handbook.

speaker: FATHER
text: I fixed his plan. Ten percent became seventy. He would have laughed.

speaker: PIP
text: A relay satellite is in your path. It will be destroyed.

speaker: PIP
text: Something is coming up behind us. It is not on any chart.

speaker: PIP
text: Departure burn done. W and S for thrust, A and D to turn. The relay is ahead.

speaker: PIP
text: Keep the relay inside the circle until the lock bar fills.

speaker: PIP
text: That relay was our only link to Earth. Nothing we send will get home now.

speaker: PIP
text: It's much faster than us. Brace!

speaker: PIP
text: They took half our supplies. The ship is lighter now, so it will accelerate faster.

speaker: PIP
text: Look at the bars and push against the spin!

speaker: PIP
text: Scanner found a planet nobody has charted. It's close enough... maybe.

speaker: PIP
text: One relay is a single point of failure. Moon radio takes 1.4 seconds one way. NASA JPL Horizons.

speaker: FATHER
text: A ship came out of nowhere and took half my supplies. It did not answer.

speaker: PIP
text: The scanner found a planet with water.

speaker: PIP
text: Pick your landing site with care. Slope, rocks and ice all matter.

speaker: PIP
text: The planet uses NASA Exoplanet Archive values: radius, starlight and temperature.

speaker: FATHER
text: The water collector is his. The footprints are fresh.

speaker: PIP
text: Solar storm. NASA's DONKI database logs flares and CMEs so crews get warning. Shield or divert?

speaker: PIP
text: Asteroid close pass. JPL close-approach data lets NASA track near-Earth objects. Dodge or hold?

speaker: PIP
text: Comms blackout. Radio travels at light speed; JPL Horizons gives the delay. Wait, or act alone?

speaker: PIP
text: Power shortfall. Sunlight fades with distance squared. NASA's Earth fact sheet: 1361 watts per square metre.

speaker: PIP
text: The survey is ready. Home is listening.

speaker: MISSION CONTROL
text: Deep Space Network. Link established.

speaker: MISSION CONTROL
text: Survey received. Every byte of it.

speaker: MISSION CONTROL
text: Coordinates, water readings... and a second flight log.

speaker: FATHER
text: He's here. He's alive.

speaker: MISSION CONTROL
text: ...Copy that. Two to bring home.

speaker: SON
text: Tell Mom I kept the water running.

speaker: MISSION CONTROL
text: The next ship is already on the build schedule. Your plan is in it.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Three NASA Deep Space Network sites keep contact as Earth turns. Source: NASA DSN, JPL.

speaker: PIP
text: Now it is your turn. Design any mission you like.
